goal: Archive terminal planning artifacts so an agent browsing docs/specs/ and docs/plans/ reaches current work instead of completed slices. Archival is a move into the existing archive/ directories, never a delete. Moving a terminal intent sidecar is provably safe rather than merely conventional: the reducer gives done and stopped no outgoing transition, so such a task can never transition again and can never need its sidecar back at the docs/plans/<task-id>.intent.json location the validator requires. Terminality must be read from two signals, not one. docs/plans/ holds 73 sidecars: 33 done, 14 stopped, 1 working, and 25 with no task record. The record-less 25 are not one kind -- canary-001 through canary-004 are fixtures named only in comment and describe labels, seventeen are older sidecars whose records were pruned or never created, and 2026-08-19-009 through 012 are complete and merged but lost their records because they were enrolled inside git worktree copies whose .imm/tasks/ never merges back. So where a record is absent, an implementing commit in Git history is the second terminality signal; anything still unresolved by both is listed as pending rather than guessed. The drafted criterion that no active spec may reference a retired tool is too broad and must be narrowed. It conflates a spec that instructs an agent to run a retired command, which is the real defect, with a spec that documents that command's retirement, which is correct and necessary. 52 active specs cite these tools, including this roadmap itself with 8 references; archiving the document governing this work, or stripping its evidence base, would be absurd. Only instructional references are in scope, and any document exempted as retirement-subject must be enumerated explicitly so the exemption cannot grow silently. Note that tests/python-reference-boundary.test.ts pins the active path docs/specs/opencode-native-plugin.spec.md, which must be updated if that spec moves.

acceptance.assertion: Every intent sidecar whose task is terminal by record phase done or stopped, or where no record exists by an implementing commit in Git history, lives under an archive directory; docs/plans/ retains only non-terminal sidecars and the canary fixtures; every move is a move and no planning artifact was deleted.

No active spec instructs running imm-plan.py, activation_plan.py, or imm-autowork, and every active document that still references them as the subject of retirement appears on an explicit enumerated exemption list.

The full suite passes, proving pinned documentation paths, notably docs/specs/opencode-native-plugin.spec.md in tests/python-reference-boundary.test.ts, were reconciled with any move rather than left dangling.
